video.title: Loops: for, range and while
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: Primary Three needed times tables, seven of them, printed for every desk. Writing them out took me a whole evening. With Python, a loop writes a times table in three lines.
Today: loops in Python, with for, range and while.

A for loop runs the same lines once for each value. Here, n takes the values one to ten, one after another. Each time round, Python prints one line of the seven times table. The indented line is the body of the loop.
range gives the numbers to loop over. range of one, eleven starts at one and stops just before eleven. So it gives one to ten. Stopping one early surprises everyone, so say it out loud.

Loops can also add things up. Start a total at zero before the loop. Inside the loop, add each value to it. After the loop, print the total. This pattern, a running total, is in nearly every useful program.

Sometimes you don’t know how many times to repeat. A while loop repeats as long as its condition is true. Here, the class saves fifty a week until it has four hundred for a football. If the condition never becomes false, the loop never ends.
Quick check! A loop uses range of one, five. Which numbers does it give?
One, two, three, four. Range stops just before the second number. To count to five, write range of one, six. This off-by-one mistake is so common it has a name.
Loops do the boring work for you. Print a times table for any number. Add up a week of rainfall. Make a numbered list of forty seats for an exam. Count down the days to the end of term.

One warning. If a while loop’s condition never becomes false, the program runs forever. On the phone, Darsi stops any program after three seconds, so nothing hangs. If that happens, check what changes inside the loop.

scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: step through a loop
scenes.narration: In the app, open Step through a program and choose A loop that adds. Before each Next, say what total will become. Then change range of one, five to range of one, eleven, and jump to the end: fifty-five.
Your turn. A loop prints one line for each value in range of zero, five. How many lines does it print?

Five. Remember: for repeats the indented lines once for each value. range stops before its second number. A running total starts at zero before the loop. And while repeats until its condition is false.

Try it in class tomorrow: Human loop. Write a for loop on the board, and let pupils be the computer: one pupil keeps the total on the board while the class reads out each value. Then change the range and run it again.

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — range stops just before the second number: 1 to 4.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — range(1, 5) starts at 1 and stops before 5: 1, 2, 3, 4.

checkpoints.prompt: A loop prints one line for each value in range(0, 5). How many lines?
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — range(0, 5) gives 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4: five values.
